title: Lokesh Kanagaraj's 'DC' Crosses ₹70 Crore Worldwide in Eight Days
excerpt: The Tamil action thriller, marking the acclaimed director's acting debut, has collected ₹44.76 crore net in India and become Kollywood's seventh-highest grosser of 2026.
body:
• DC has crossed ₹70 crore in worldwide gross collections after eight days, with ₹44.76 crore net domestically — making it Kollywood's seventh-highest grosser of 2026.
  • The film marks Lokesh Kanagaraj's acting debut alongside Wamiqa Gabbi, directed by Arun Matheswaran and produced by Sun Pictures.
  • Kerala has consistently outperformed Tamil Nadu at the box office from Day 5 onward, an unusual pattern for a Tamil-origin film.
  • With a production budget of ₹25 crore, DC has already recouped its costs multiple times over and is being hailed as a blockbuster.

Lokesh Kanagaraj's acting debut DC (also known as DC: The Bloody Valentine) has sailed past the ₹70 crore mark in worldwide gross collections after eight days in theatres, according to data from industry tracker Sacnilk. The Tamil action thriller has now collected ₹44.76 crore net at the Indian box office, making it Kollywood's seventh-highest grosser of 2026.

A Steady Climb

Unlike most Tamil releases that see a sharp post-opening-weekend drop, DC has defied industry norms with remarkably stable daily collections. The film opened to ₹4.4 crore net on August 7 — a modest start for a film anchored by a first-time actor — but audience word-of-mouth sent numbers climbing.

By Sunday, Day 3, the film posted its best single-day haul at ₹9.55 crore net, bringing the opening weekend total to ₹20.95 crore — the sixth-highest Kollywood opening weekend of 2026. The weekday collections held strong, with Day 5 seeing India gross reach ₹37.21 crore and the worldwide total crossing the ₹50 crore milestone.

On Day 6, the first Wednesday of its run, the film earned ₹5 crore net — a minor 9.9 percent drop from the previous day — pushing India net to ₹37.50 crore and worldwide gross to ₹58.62 crore across 25,645 shows.

Kerala Leads the Charge

The most striking aspect of DC's box office story is its state-wise performance. From Day 5 onward, Kerala has consistently outperformed Tamil Nadu — an unusual feat for a Tamil-origin film. On Day 6, Kerala recorded ₹1.94 crore gross compared to Tamil Nadu's ₹1.60 crore, showcasing the massive pull Lokesh Kanagaraj commands in the Kerala market.

Andhra Pradesh and Telangana have also emerged as strong territories, contributing ₹1.40 crore on Day 6 — nearly matching Tamil Nadu's numbers. The Telugu version has netted ₹9.85 crore overall, while the Hindi version has added ₹2.15 crore.

Already a Blockbuster

Against a production budget of approximately ₹25 crore, DC had recouped over 83 percent of its costs through domestic theatrical revenue within the opening weekend alone. The film has since crossed the break-even mark several times over.

On BookMyShow, DC became the 25th Tamil film since August 2023 to sell over one million tickets, reaching 1.12 million within six days. Kochi led multiplex occupancy with a 65.5 percent average, with night shows hitting a staggering 82 percent across 137 shows.

What Makes DC Different

Directed by Arun Matheswaran and produced by Sun Pictures, DC follows two outcasts — Devadas (Lokesh Kanagaraj) and Chandra (Wamiqa Gabbi) — on a violent run from a vengeful police officer. The A-certified film features a score by Anirudh Ravichander and uses high-contrast black-and-white visuals for its action sequences.

The film's continued strong performance is notable given the competitive landscape heading into the Independence Day weekend, with new releases including Suriya's Vishwanath & Sons and Vishal's Magudam vying for screens. For diaspora audiences who have been following Lokesh Kanagaraj's career since Kaithi and the Lokesh Cinematic Universe, DC represents a fascinating new chapter for one of Tamil cinema's most bankable filmmakers.
